summary: Implemented the chain-agnostic PoolIdentity(chain_id, pool_id, pool_manager_address) value object as the post-amendment T011 contract requires. PoolIdentity is a frozen slotted dataclass in src/robinhood_lp/protocol/identity.py that stores the on-chain V4 PoolId byte-for-byte (keccak256 of the ABI-encoded PoolKey), validates the three required fields at construction (no defaults, no fallback for pool_manager_address), supports round-trip through (chain_id, pool_id, pool_manager_address), and treats equality/hash on all three fields. The type is chain-agnostic on day one: construction succeeds for ChainId(1), the Owner-confirmed placeholder ChainId(46630), and any sentinel ChainId; cross-chain collision tests use the placeholder. Re-exported from src/robinhood_lp/protocol/__init__.py. Added 14 new tests in tests/test_protocol_identity.py covering construction-without-pool_manager rejection, round-trip, equality and hash on all three fields, byte-exact preservation of the V4 keccak256 PoolId, cross-chain collision prevention at ChainId(1) vs ChainId(46630), and the chain-agnostic property. All four quality commands run twice with byte-identical output: pytest '329 passed, 2 skipped', ruff check 'All checks passed!', ruff format --check '160 files already formatted', mypy 'Success: no issues found in 41 source files'. No pre-existing tests or implementation files outside the planned scope were modified; the existing tests/test_protocol_events.py and src/robinhood_lp/protocol/{ids,abi,math,events}.py are untouched.

residual_risks: The Owner-confirmed placeholder ChainId(46630) is used in cross-chain collision tests until T024 verifies the real Robinhood Chain chain id. The type itself is chain-agnostic and does not embed any chain-specific value, so swapping to the real chain id later is a constant change in the tests only.

PoolIdentity does not provide a convenience constructor with a default pool_manager_address, by contract. Production code MUST pass an explicit pool_manager_address; this is enforced by the dataclass field requirement and by tests/test_protocol_identity.py::test_pool_identity_required_pool_manager_address.

The Developer role runs pytest with PYTHONPATH=src (the worktree's src) so that the worktree implementation is tested, matching the convention used by prior T001/T002/T003 developer attempts captured in todo/evidence/P00/.

The PoolIdentity.does_not_replace_pool_id invariant is asserted at the value-object level only (the on-chain PoolId is stored byte-for-byte). If downstream code later constructs PoolIdentity from a PoolKey without first deriving the canonical PoolId, that is a caller-side bug, not a PoolIdentity defect; the type does not accept a PoolKey directly and therefore cannot silently re-derive.
